text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ

words.gloss_range: conjunctive/result prefix marking the scene as a consequence-bearing continuation
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the scene a consequence-bearing continuation from the prior confrontation. Its single-letter prefix is fused to the temporal hinge, so sequence and consequence arrive before the violence is even quoted.

topics.headline: sequence and consequence prefix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse opens as the next consequence after truth confronts power, not as a self-contained report.
topics.reason: The conjunctive/result prefix is fused to the temporal opening and the clause evidence marks the opening as the temporal trigger from the prior discourse.

topics.headline: fused boundary movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the transition carried in a single prefixed letter before the temporal hinge unfolds.
topics.reason: The surface is a one-letter proclitic attached to the following temporal particle.

words.gloss_range: temporal trigger once the arrival is complete; not an unresolved not-yet sense
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) makes the arrival clause a completed trigger. The main event is therefore the exposed answer to truth, and the compact opening hinge carries the prior scene into this command scene.

topics.headline: completed arrival as trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hostile command is the exposed answer to a completed arrival of truth.
topics.reason: The particle subordinates the perfect arrival clause before the main speech response.

topics.headline: compact sequential hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening as a compact stage boundary from the previous ayah into this reaction scene.
topics.reason: The temporal particle receives sequence force from the prefixed particle before it.

words.gloss_range: completed arrival or presentation reaching the opponents directly before their speech
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, bringing, or presenting; local frame selects evidentiary arrival with an object pronoun and a proof phrase
words.prose: {{ar:جَآءَهُم}} ({{tr:jāʾahum}}) makes the opponents the reached recipients before they become speakers. The perfect arrival, with proof carried in the following phrase, makes the command reactive to accomplished evidentiary confrontation; 10:76 shows accusation as one response to truth-arrival, while this ayah escalates into demographic orders and 40:78 later turns arrival language toward decree.

topics.headline: opponents directly reached
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the later speakers first become direct recipients of the truth, so their order follows contact rather than rumor.
topics.reason: The attached plural object pronoun is the object or recipient of the coming verb.

topics.headline: arrival as proof-presentation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees truth entering first as accomplished evidentiary confrontation, with hostile speech only afterward.
topics.reason: The perfect verb precedes the speech verb and governs the proof phrase through the attached preposition.

topics.headline: truth-arrival echoes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 10:76, where truth-arrival is answered by accusation, and 40:78, where arrival language moves toward decree.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete parallels that illuminate escalation without replacing the local parse.

words.gloss_range: attached preposition making the truth the carried content, means, or accompaniment of the coming
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the truth to the coming as carried content, means, and accompaniment. Because it is a proclitic, the proof is not a loose afterthought but attached tightly to the arrival frame.

topics.headline: truth attached as content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coming is not bare motion; the truth is carried as content and proof with it.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the truth noun with the coming verb, licensing content, accompaniment, and instrumental force.

topics.headline: tight proclitic attachment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the proof phrase bound tightly at the word edge rather than left as a loose afterthought.
topics.reason: The preposition is a bound proclitic on the following noun.

words.gloss_range: definite established truth or binding reality, governed after the attached preposition and qualified by divine provenance
words.root_gloss_range: truth, reality, right, due claim, firmness, and realization; local use selects established revealed reality with binding force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: doubled letter in the local word, used only for recitational sound pressure

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَقِّ}} ({{tr:al-ḥaqqi}}) is definite, stable, and binding: the opponents answer established reality rather than an optional claim. The source phrase completes its provenance before the quote begins, and the ayah then frames the middle commands between truth at the opening and lostness at the close; 17:81 makes truth-arrival expel falsehood, while here it exposes falsehood as coercive policy. The doubled {{ar:ق}} ({{tr:qāf}}) gives the truth noun audible firmness at the point where firmness is semantically central, and that sound pressure remains recitational texture rather than a separate lexical branch.

topics.headline: definite binding reality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what arrives is identifiable binding reality, not an optional claim awaiting enemy validation.
topics.reason: The definite gerund/noun after the attached preposition selects stable presented truth with obligation and firmness pressure.

topics.headline: truth completed by source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees content and divine provenance completed before the hostile quote is allowed to begin.
topics.reason: The truth noun is governed after the attached preposition and then qualified by the source phrase.

topics.headline: truth-to-lostness frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader reads the violent commands between the opening pole of truth and the closing pole of lostness.
topics.reason: The word stands in the temporal trigger before the quote, while the final verdict supplies the contrasting endpoint.

topics.headline: truth exposes falsehood differently
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast 17:81, where truth arrival expels falsehood, with 40:25, where truth arrival exposes falsehood as coercive policy.
topics.reason: The source rows supply the concrete 17:81 comparison and the local structure supports a reaction reading.

topics.headline: recitational firmness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the doubled {{ar:ق}} ({{tr:qāf}}) making the truth noun phonetically firm at the point where firmness is semantically central, while the lexical sense remains governed by truth and binding reality.
topics.reason: The sound rows are useful as recitational texture, but they do not create an independent semantic branch.

words.gloss_range: source preposition opening the provenance phrase and excluding a loose partitive reading here
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) opens the source phrase and marks provenance from divine custody. Its separate form slows the opening just enough to specify origin before the hostile quote begins.

topics.headline: source from divine custody
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the truth is explicitly sourced before any enemy words appear.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the divine-nearness phrase as source, not partitive residue.

topics.headline: separate source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a small syntactic pause that opens provenance before the quote begins.
topics.reason: Unlike the earlier bound preposition, this separate preposition opens a new source phrase.

words.gloss_range: from divine nearness, custody, possession, and authority as the source of the truth
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, possession, presence, and source-at; local phrase marks first-person divine provenance
words.prose: {{ar:عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) makes the provenance first-person divine, a source in nearness, possession, and authority outside enemy control. Its placement directly before the speech verb makes the command answer explicitly sourced truth; 10:76 uses the same provenance pressure before a magic charge, and this ayah moves from near source to a plot enclosed in lostness.

topics.headline: first-person divine provenance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the truth comes from divine possession and nearness, outside enemy control.
topics.reason: The word is the governed complement of the source preposition and carries the attached first-person plural suffix.

topics.headline: provenance borders hostile speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees hostile speech begin only after source authority has been placed at the threshold.
topics.reason: The provenance phrase closes the opening trigger immediately before the speech verb.

topics.headline: same provenance formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 10:76, where the same divine-provenance formula is answered with a magic charge, to the harder policy response here.
topics.reason: The concrete 10:76 rows show the formula as a repeated pressure point in rejection scenes.

topics.headline: nearness contrasted with lostness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from authoritative nearness at the source to lostness as the plot domain.
topics.reason: The source phrase in the opening and the locative verdict in the closing create a local contrast.

words.gloss_range: completed collective saying that introduces executable imperatives as quoted policy
words.root_gloss_range: saying, declaring, claiming, or commanding; local quote frame makes speech function as public order
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) gives the reached opponents a completed collective voice. Because the quote contains two imperatives, saying becomes policy issuance rather than mere opinion; 10:76 keeps the response at accusation, while 40:25 turns it into orders and 40:26-28 keeps speech and killing in controversy.

topics.headline: collective completed speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a collective factional voice issuing two imperatives as one quoted policy.
topics.reason: The perfect plural speech verb introduces the imperative quote as its complement.

topics.headline: saying becomes policy issuance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees speech become an administrative act that moves denial from accusation into bodies.
topics.reason: The quoted content consists of commands, so the saying functions as policy issuance in this frame.

topics.headline: speech response escalates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast 10:76 with the escalation in 40:25 and then watch q-w-l and q-t-l continue through 40:26-28.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete parallel and same-passage references for escalation.

words.gloss_range: direct Form I plural imperative to kill, with the sons as explicit patient class rather than reciprocal combatants
words.root_gloss_range: killing, slaying, fighting in licensed derived forms, and death-related force; local Form I imperative selects direct killing
words.prose: {{ar:ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:uqtulū}}) opens the quote as a direct Form I plural imperative, with the sons as patients rather than combatants. The command voices a Pharaohic oppression pattern seen in 2:49 and continues into the {{ar:ق ت ل}} ({{tr:q-t-l}}) dispute of 40:26, while its pairing with the life command makes death and controlled survival two tools of one policy; the hard stop texture of this killing command also contrasts with the breathier flow of the following life-root command.

topics.headline: direct lethal imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quote opens with direct executable killing aimed at a patient class, not reciprocal battle.
topics.reason: The local Form I plural imperative governs the sons as explicit direct object.

topics.headline: oppression pattern voiced as command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 2:49, where son-slaughter is narrated as oppression, with 40:25, where the oppressors voice the command themselves and the q-t-l controversy continues in 40:26.
topics.reason: The echo rows provide concrete oppression and next-ayah references without changing the local imperative parse.

topics.headline: death paired with controlled life
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees death and controlled survival as paired tools in one demographic policy.
topics.reason: The first imperative is coordinated with a second life-root imperative and the objects form a gendered pair.

words.gloss_range: plural sons or male descendants as the first direct object, defined by the believing group and treated as lineage continuity under attack
words.root_gloss_range: building, forming, sons, descendants, and lineage continuity; local plural noun selects sons while retaining future-continuity pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أَبْنَآءَ}} ({{tr:abnāʾa}}) is the first direct object under the killing command, a plural successor cohort rather than a single target. The root pressure of building and lineage makes the attack feel aimed at future continuity, while the relative clause defines those sons by allegiance; 2:49 and 14:6 stand behind the recurring Pharaohic targeting of sons, and the later women-object balances them as a paired social policy.

topics.headline: sons under lethal action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sons as a plural successor cohort placed directly under the killing command.
topics.reason: The noun is the accusative direct object of the first imperative and its plural form gives collective target scope.

topics.headline: lineage future under attack
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the attack on future continuity, while the local noun remains sons rather than a free building metaphor.
topics.reason: The root evidence can pressure continuity, but local grammar selects the kinship noun.

topics.headline: target defined by allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sons are targeted through the believing group and their allegiance, not through a separate named crime.
topics.reason: The following relative clause structurally defines the first object before the second imperative begins.

topics.headline: recurring son-targeting pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear 2:49 and 14:6 behind the command, where sons are a recurring Pharaohic target.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete prior references for the pattern.

topics.headline: sons balanced with women
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one community divided into a killed future and controlled survivors.
topics.reason: The sons begin the first object slot and are balanced by the possessed women in the second.

words.gloss_range: plural relative pronoun defining the targeted group by the following faith-alignment clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) delays completion of the target and turns the object into a defined victim class. The sons are not merely named; they are linked to those whose faith-alignment the next words specify.

topics.headline: relative clause builds victim class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the target is not complete at sons; the relative pronoun delays completion until faith-alignment defines the class.
topics.reason: The plural masculine relative pronoun is in genitive dependence after the sons and introduces the identifying clause.

words.gloss_range: Form IV plural belief or trust-commitment, objectless and specified by accompaniment with him
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, faith, safekeeping, and commitment; local Form IV selects believing allegiance under threat
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) makes the relative clause name the alleged offense: belief with him, without any separate crime. The root field lets this belief feel like trust-commitment under violence, and 7:123 clarifies how Pharaohic power treats unauthorized faith as political loyalty; within the ayah, trust identity is later opposed by covering identity.

topics.headline: belief as allegiance with him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no separate crime is named; belief with him functions as the identifying charge.
topics.reason: The Form IV plural verb agrees with the relative pronoun, lacks an overt object, and is followed by the accompaniment phrase.

topics.headline: trust turned into targeted commitment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels faith as trust-commitment under violence, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as believing allegiance.
topics.reason: The root field supplies trust and security pressure, but the local Form IV clause selects committed belief.

topics.headline: belief treated as unauthorized loyalty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 7:123, where belief before permission is treated as political threat, with the targeting of belief with him here.
topics.reason: The source rows give the concrete 7:123 comparison.

topics.headline: faith opposed to covering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah set trust identity against covering identity before the final verdict names the plotters.
topics.reason: The believing group in the object phrase is later opposed by the disbeliever class in the final construct.

words.gloss_range: with him as accompaniment and allegiance, with the pronoun making Moses the alignment pole
words.prose: {{ar:مَعَهُۥ}} ({{tr:maʿahū}}) specifies belief as alignment with him. The attached pronoun fuses Moses into the phrase as the pole around whom the targeted allegiance gathers.

topics.headline: Moses as alignment pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that faith is specified as alignment with him, so the political target is allegiance around Moses.
topics.reason: The adverbial phrase modifies the belief verb and carries an attached masculine singular pronoun as the alignment pole.

words.gloss_range: coordinating prefix joining the second imperative to the first as one paired command policy
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the second imperative to the first. The conjunction carries addition with contrast, so the life-command is paired with killing inside one policy rather than separated as mercy.

topics.headline: second command coordinated to first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second imperative joined to the first as a matched policy, not as a separate act of mercy.
topics.reason: The conjunction is prefixed to the second imperative and coordinates it with the killing command.

words.gloss_range: Form X plural imperative to keep alive or spare, locally coercive rather than merciful or life-giving
words.root_gloss_range: life, vitality, living, modesty-related derivatives, and keeping alive; local Form X selects imposed preservation
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَحْيُوا۟}} ({{tr:istaḥyū}}) is a Form X imperative of keeping alive, governing the women as its object. The life-root becomes controlled survival rather than mercy or life-giving; 28:4 describes the same Pharaohic sparing pattern, while this verse voices it as command, completing the death-command by deciding who remains under control.

topics.headline: survival imposed by command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that keeping alive is an imposed directive over the women, not passive mercy or divine life-giving.
topics.reason: The Form X plural imperative governs the women as direct object and differs from simple revivification.

topics.headline: life-root made coercive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the life-root turned into controlled survival, while local grammar keeps the selected action as keeping alive.
topics.reason: The lexical field supplies life and modesty pressure, but the hostile imperative frame narrows it to coercive preservation.

topics.headline: sparing pattern voiced as command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 28:4, where Pharaoh is described as sparing women, with 40:25, where the same logic is voiced as an imperative.
topics.reason: The source rows provide the concrete 28:4 echo.

topics.headline: life command completes death command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the life command complete the death command by deciding who remains under control.
topics.reason: The second imperative is coordinated with the first within one quoted command unit.

words.gloss_range: their women, wives, or female members as a possessed plural object under the second imperative
words.root_gloss_range: women, wives, or female collective; local possessed plural marks the women of the believing group as an affected social segment
words.prose: {{ar:نِسَآءَهُمْ}} ({{tr:nisāʾahum}}) ties the women to the same believing group through the attached plural suffix. Its range can include women, wives, or female kin, but the hostile possessed-object frame makes them an affected social segment; 2:49, 7:127, and 28:4 show the women-and-sons pair as a recurring domination pattern, and this second object closes the quoted policy.

topics.headline: women tied to believers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possessed suffix ties the women to the same believing group whose sons were targeted.
topics.reason: The noun is the direct object of the second imperative and its attached plural pronoun resumes the targeted community.

topics.headline: women or wives as social segment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the range women, wives, or female kin in view, while the hostile possessive object frame makes them an affected social segment.
topics.reason: The local possessed plural does not force a single narrower English term, but it does keep the range communal and affected.

topics.headline: women and sons pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 2:49, 7:127, and 28:4, where women and sons recur as paired targets of Pharaohic domination.
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete references for the repeated gendered pair.

topics.headline: second object closes policy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second object close the command pair, making the policy gendered rather than generically punitive.
topics.reason: The object fills the second imperative slot and mirrors the sons as paired objects.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction pivoting from the quote into the narrator verdict
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots out of enemy speech into the narrator verdict. The quote is not allowed to stand last; the linked evaluation immediately undercuts it.

topics.headline: quote pivots into narrator verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command does not stand last; the conjunction immediately pivots into an evaluative verdict.
topics.reason: The conjunction prefixed to the negation links the verdict to the quote while shifting speaker frame.

words.gloss_range: negative particle beginning a negation-exception restriction over the final nominal sentence
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) begins the restriction that denies the plot every predicate except containment in lostness. Because the clause is nominal, the verdict reads as standing classification, not another narrated event.

topics.headline: negation-exception restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees every imagined predicate for the plot collapse into one verdict: containment in lostness.
topics.reason: The negative particle works with the later exception particle over the nominal sentence.

topics.headline: standing classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close classifies the plot as a standing condition rather than narrating another event.
topics.reason: The final clause is nominal and negated.

words.gloss_range: stratagem or hostile contrivance gathered as a nominative construct subject for judgment
words.root_gloss_range: plotting, stratagem, contrivance, forceful handling, and other construction-bound branches; local gerund selects calculated hostile scheme
words.prose: {{ar:كَيْدُ}} ({{tr:kaydu}}) gathers the two imperatives into one judged scheme owned by the disbelieving class. The word names calculated hostile contrivance rather than rage, and 105:2 offers a concrete echo where hostile plotting is placed in misdirection; 40:37 keeps the same-surah thread of exposed maneuvering, while the final cadence slows into verdict.

topics.headline: commands gathered as plot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two concrete commands are reclassified as one judged strategy.
topics.reason: The gerund construct is the nominative subject of the final nominal sentence and governs the disbeliever class.

topics.headline: calculated hostile maneuver
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the policy as calculated contrivance rather than uncontrolled rage.
topics.reason: The local noun selects the stratagem branch of the root family.

topics.headline: plot placed in misdirection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 105:2, where hostile plotting is put in misdirection, with 40:25 locating the scheme inside lostness.
topics.reason: The source rows give the concrete 105:2 echo and the local predicate is a lostness container.

topics.headline: plotting recurs in the surah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track 40:37 as a same-surah return where apparent maneuvering is exposed as futile strategy.
topics.reason: The source row gives the concrete same-surah recurrence.

topics.headline: slower nominal cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the movement slow from command rhythm into measured verdict cadence.
topics.reason: The final nominal clause differs rhythmically from the quoted imperatives.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle plural naming the plot-owning class by ongoing covering or denial
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denial, disbelief, ingratitude, seed-covering, expiation, and other branch-specific senses; local active participle selects disbelieving coverers of truth
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-kāfirīna}}) makes the plot belong to a definite disbelieving class. The active participle names an ongoing covering identity after truth has arrived; 57:20 preserves a concrete seed-coverer image, but here the local sense is moral denial, set against those who believed and carried toward the same lost end seen again in 40:50.

topics.headline: definite class owns the plot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final verdict generalize from the quoted speakers to the definite disbelieving class that owns the plot.
topics.reason: The definite plural active participle is the construct complement of the plot noun.

topics.headline: ongoing covering identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the violent response named as an identity of covering and denial after revealed truth has arrived.
topics.reason: The active participle form names ongoing agentive identity, and the local context follows the arrival of truth.

topics.headline: concrete covering image moralized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 57:20, where the coverer image is concrete, while 40:25 moralizes covering as suppressing truth through violence.
topics.reason: The agricultural branch is valid as background image, but the local participle selects disbelieving denial.

topics.headline: faith and disbelief opposed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah oppose the victims named by faith to the plotters named by covering.
topics.reason: The object phrase names those who believed, and the final construct names the plot owners by disbelief.

topics.headline: strategy and prayer share lost end
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect 40:50 with 40:25 as a same-surah pattern where disbelievers strategy and supplication share a lost end.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete same-surah comparison.

words.gloss_range: exception particle completing restriction and leaving only the lostness predicate
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes the restriction rather than introducing an ordinary listed exception. After alternatives are denied, only the lostness predicate remains for the plot.

topics.headline: exception leaves one predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception particle does not add a normal exception member; it completes the restriction that leaves only lostness for the plot.
topics.reason: The particle works with the prior negation before the predicate phrase.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition making lostness the domain or container of the plot
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes lostness the container or domain of the plot, not merely a result reached later. Its separate prepositional beat delays the final noun so the verdict lands with force.

topics.headline: plot inside lostness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lostness is not merely the later result; it is the domain containing the plot.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the lostness noun and the prepositional phrase serves as the restricted predicate.

topics.headline: final noun delayed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the preposition briefly delay the final verdict word so lostness lands last.
topics.reason: The independent preposition creates a short beat before its complement.

words.gloss_range: indefinite lostness, error, or path-failure as the final restricted predicate domain
words.root_gloss_range: wandering, losing the way, error, misdirection, and loss; local noun names the state or domain containing the plot
words.prose: {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍۢ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}) completes the only predicate left: an indefinite state of lostness and path-failure. The final lexical landing is not enemy policy but its failure; 105:2 gives a concrete misdirection echo, and the close answers the opening truth by moving from firmness into path-loss.

topics.headline: only predicate domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the plot classified compactly as an indefinite state or kind of lostness.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the locative preposition and completes the only predicate left by restriction.

topics.headline: path-loss as final verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the last lexical landing as wandering, error, and path-failure rather than enemy policy.
topics.reason: The root field supports path-loss and the word occupies final lexical position.

topics.headline: hostile plots misdirected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 105:2, where hostile plots are rendered misdirected, with this ayah closing the scheme inside lostness.
topics.reason: The source rows supply the concrete 105:2 echo.

topics.headline: closing answers opening truth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the movement from established truth at the opening to path-loss at the close.
topics.reason: The opening truth term and final lostness term frame the ayah movement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence جَاءَهُم بِالْحَقِّ ... قَالُوا اقْتُلُوا ... وَاسْتَحْيُوا anchors a spoken policy directly to the truth's arrival.
baseline_models.mechanism: Arrival, speech, killing, and deliberate non-killing form one reaction chain. The response does not merely reject a proposition; it converts rejection into an asymmetric allocation of death and continued life.

activation_trace.role: Coming and becoming present supplies the event that triggers the reaction chain.
Truth fixed against falsehood supplies the resistant reality that has arrived.
Uttered speech turns the reaction into an explicit executable command.
Taking life supplies the lethal side of the ordered sorting.
Keeping alive and refraining from killing supplies the deliberately preserved side of the same sorting.

changed_reading.before: They rejected the truth and persecuted its followers.
changed_reading.after: The truth's arrival immediately elicited a voiced sorting policy that assigned death to one group and continued life to another.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The command targets أَبْنَاءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ while preserving نِسَاءَهُمْ, not an undifferentiated population.
baseline_models.mechanism: Sons carry the branch image of descent from a source, while women are retained as a distinct group. The death/life asymmetry therefore attacks the believers' lineal continuation and social composition, whether or not that was its only immediate purpose.

activation_trace.role: Sonship, descent, and attribution to an origin make the killed group the believers' lineal continuation.
Heart-settled assent marks the parent community whose continuation is being selected against.
Purposeful preservation from killing makes survival an imposed policy rather than incidental escape.
The collective of women supplies the explicitly retained demographic category.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports a cruel but generic act of persecution.
changed_reading.after: The verse reports a calibrated assault on a believing community's descent and composition: its sons are removed while its women are deliberately retained.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَمَا كَيْدُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ places the agents' stratagem inside ضلال rather than merely labeling it wicked.
baseline_models.mechanism: Those who cover the truth apply an intense contrivance, but the contrivance is enclosed in deviation and loss. Its violence may be effective locally while the plan as a plan cannot find or retain its intended destination.

activation_trace.role: Scheming and contrivance supply the organized design behind the selective violence.
Covering supplies the agents' functional relation to the truth they seek to suppress.
Blocking or denying truth specifies what the covering accomplishes in this conflict.
Deviation from the intended path makes the strategy directionally defective.
Loss of the sought object makes failure internal to the stratagem rather than an external moral comment.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers' plot is condemned as misguided.
changed_reading.after: Their organized suppression is itself pathless: even when it inflicts harm, it loses the end for which it was designed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, truth is paired with decisive judgment, and the coming of God's command culminates in judgment by truth. This revises the focus arrival from delivery of correct information toward the onset of a reality that exposes and decides, making the kill order a defensive reaction to impending adjudication.

activation_trace.role: The truth's coming supplies the focus event whose force is revised by later judgment sequences.
Fixed truth supplies the reality that the coercive response cannot alter.
The paired presence and absence of decisive judgment makes truth the criterion of operative ruling.
Truth explicitly accompanies God's judging, activating a judicial dimension in the focus truth.
The command's coming repeats the arrival pattern at the moment of final decision.
The arriving affair supplies the enacted event rather than a merely debated claim.
Decisive judgment supplies the consequence of that arrival.
Truth again qualifies the judgment, closing the arrival-to-verdict mechanism.

structural_cues: 40:20 opposes God's judging by truth to others' inability to judge anything.
40:78 orders coming command, judgment by truth, and the loss of falsifiers in one sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated arrival, truth, command, and judgment links; I infer that 40:25's arrival begins adjudicative exposure. A live alternative is that the focus phrase denotes revelation alone and the judicial force is only a later echo.

changed_reading.before: Correct teaching arrived, and the rulers answered it with violence.
changed_reading.after: An exposing and ultimately decisive truth arrived, and the rulers answered the onset of that verdict with violence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier national pattern joins resolved intention, seizure of messengers, false disputation, and attempted displacement of truth. The focus kill order is therefore one local execution of a recurring suppression script in which bodily capture and argumentative destabilization serve the same end.

activation_trace.role: Contrived scheming names the focus policy as designed action rather than spontaneous rage.
An intention contracted in the self supplies the planning stage of the recurring script.
Seizure and capture supply coercive control of the messenger and its reversing consequence.
Loss of truth and stability supplies the false medium used in the dispute.
Making an argument fall supplies the intended displacement of truth.
Fixed truth is the common object that both coercion and false disputation try to remove.

structural_cues: 40:5 moves from communal resolve to seize a messenger, then from false disputation to attempted displacement of truth.
40:25 similarly moves from truth's arrival to a communal command of coercive violence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two ordered suppression sequences; I infer that capture, debate, and selective killing are substitutable instruments in one recurring mechanism. The alternative is a looser historical analogy without a unified operational script.

changed_reading.before: The focus records an isolated tyrannical reaction.
changed_reading.after: The focus instantiates a repeatable regime script: plan, seize or kill, and use coercion or false argument to displace an arriving truth.

context_deltas.mechanism: The threatened sons are later counterposed by the children of Israel inheriting the Book and by the surah's full child-to-maturity arc. The order can thus be read as an attempt to interrupt biological and textual succession, while the surah portrays the attacked line as continuing into inheritance and maturity.

activation_trace.role: Descent from a source makes the killed sons bear the threatened line of continuation.
Taking life supplies the attempted break in that continuation.
Transmission of knowledge or Book as inheritance supplies a continuation that outlives the coercive order.
The children named by descent reappear as the receiving collective rather than an extinguished line.
The small child supplies the beginning of the developmental continuity targeted in the focus.
Reaching full strength supplies the maturation endpoint that killing sons attempts to prevent.

structural_cues: 40:53 places guidance, inheritance, children, and Book in one compact statement.
40:67 explicitly sequences origin, child, full strength, old age, and appointed term.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies threatened sons, later children inheriting the Book, and an intact maturation sequence; I infer an attempted severing of communal transmission. Immediate terror, labor control, or political intimidation remain materially live alternative purposes.

changed_reading.before: The sons are victims within a moment of persecution.
changed_reading.after: The sons embody a succession the regime tries to cut, while the surah answers with an inheriting line and a protected arc from child to maturity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus disbelievers cover truth through public coercion, while a believer inside Pharaoh's people temporarily conceals faith, then voices an objection and is protected. Concealment is split by function: one covering suppresses truth and life; the other preserves a bearer until testimony can emerge.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the suppressive action named by the focus agents.
Believing assent marks the community whose truth and lives are being suppressed.
Hiding and covering supply a protective, temporary mode of concealment inside Pharaoh's own people.
Belief and the concealed faith keep the hidden content continuous with the focus believers.
Protection that repels harm completes the preservation function of the hidden believer's trajectory.

structural_cues: 40:28 identifies a believer within Pharaoh's people, states that he conceals faith, and then gives him public speech against killing.
40:45 later states that he is protected from the evils of their devising.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies coercive covering, concealed faith, subsequent speech, and protection; I infer two ethically opposed technologies of concealment. The alternative is that the hidden faith is individual prudence without a deliberate counter-mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Disbelief and belief are opposing convictions in the focus conflict.
changed_reading.after: They also generate opposed uses of covering: power covers truth by violence, while hidden faith preserves a truthful witness inside power's own house.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus formula is echoed by Pharaoh's plot being only in ruin, followed by the evil of devising descending around Pharaoh's people; even the disbelievers' later call is only in error. The plot's ضلال is thus not inactivity but a process that misses its end and folds its harm back around its makers.

activation_trace.role: The focus scheme supplies the designed process whose trajectory is tested by the later echoes.
Deviation from destination supplies the focus judgment on that trajectory.
Pharaoh's named scheme directly repeats and localizes the focus stratagem.
Loss and destruction give the repeated formula an explicit failed endpoint.
Descending evil that surrounds its target supplies the plot's reflexive return around Pharaoh's people.
Calling and attempted verbal reach supply another operation that fails to arrive at its desired response.
The repeated in-error formula extends pathlessness from coercive plotting to futile calling.

structural_cues: 40:25 and 40:37 share the construction that a plot is only in a failed state.
40:45 reverses direction by placing the encircling evil of the devising upon Pharaoh's people.
40:50 repeats the only-in-error construction for the disbelievers' call.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel formulas, an explicit ruin term, and an encircling reversal; I infer directional and reflexive failure. A live alternative is that each formula independently states eventual judgment without describing one shared causal geometry.

changed_reading.before: The plot is misguided and will ultimately fail.
changed_reading.after: The plot moves, harms, and organizes, yet cannot reach its intended end; its trajectory bends into ruin and surrounding harm for its makers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus regime uses sex and relation to believers to allocate death and survival. The later male-or-female believer formula instead joins both sexes under one condition of faithful good action and one outcome. The two passages enact rival systems for classifying human worth and destiny.

activation_trace.role: Male descendants supply the category marked for death by the coercive classification.
The collective of women supplies the category marked for imposed survival.
The male category is placed inside a shared moral conditional rather than assigned a separate fate.
The female category is paired with the male under the same moral conditional.
Believing assent supplies the shared condition that displaces the regime's sex-based allocation.
Right action supplies the evaluative criterion applied equally across the paired sexes.

structural_cues: 40:25 assigns opposite immediate outcomes to sons and women.
40:40 coordinates male and female under the same faith-and-action condition and the same promised entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two explicit gender pairings with opposed allocation rules; I infer a deliberate contrast between coercive demographic valuation and shared moral agency. The alternative is that 40:40 is generally inclusive without directly answering 40:25's policy.

changed_reading.before: The focus order is a gender-selective tactic of persecution.
changed_reading.after: The order also exposes a rival regime of valuation: tyranny sorts sexes into death and survival, while the surah later gives male and female the same moral agency and horizon.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it crosses from sonship to architecture through one root inventory. It remains anchored in focus أَبْنَاء and the later imperative to build, but downstream prose should present it as root-image resonance, not claim that أَبْنَاء literally means buildings.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus root ب ن ي names the sons selected for destruction; 40:36 uses the same root for Pharaoh's command to build a tower.

activation_trace.role: Sonship and descent supply the living construction of a continuing community.
Joining parts into a structure activates the exploratory building image within the word for sons.
The command to construct supplies Pharaoh's competing investment in an engineered material structure.
The high building specifies the monumental form of the structure Pharaoh chooses to raise.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh destroys sons in one episode and orders a tower in another.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, power destroys the believers' living architecture of descent while commanding that its own monumental architecture be raised.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because the focus uses prepositional عِند while the inventory also carries an obduracy branch. It remains anchored through repeated ع ن د occurrences that contrast truth from near Us with knowledge held near them; render it only as an epistemic and root-sound resonance, not as a syntactic derivation of obstinacy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The truth comes مِنْ عِندِنَا in 40:25, while 40:83 depicts people rejoicing in the knowledge عِندَهُم before the mocked consequence surrounds them.

activation_trace.role: Nearness and presence locate the truth's source as what is with Us.
Obdurate resistance to known truth supplies a contained exploratory shadow, not the direct sense of the preposition.
Nearness in judgment places the unsupported disputation before both God and the believers.
What is held near them supplies a rival, possessed epistemic center.
Knowledge disclosed to its knower specifies the content in which they rejoice.
The surrounding descent of what was mocked exposes the limit of their at-hand knowledge.

changed_reading.before: Truth from God confronts people who reject it.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the conflict is also between rival epistemic nearnesses: truth from what is with Us and confidence in what is merely held with them.

strongest_changes: Truth's arrival became the onset of exposure and judgment, not only delivery of correct information.
The selective killing became an attempted break in communal succession, answered by inherited Book and an intact child-to-maturity arc.
The plot's location in ضلال became operational pathlessness and reflexive failure, not only moral condemnation.
Concealment split into violent covering of truth and protective concealment of faith within Pharaoh's own people.
The male-female contrast exposed rival systems for assigning human worth and outcome.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah repetitions align arrival, truth, judgment, plotting, ruin, and reversal, while the ب ن ي network unexpectedly juxtaposes destroyed sons, inheriting children, and Pharaoh's commanded tower.
remaining_uncertainties: The lineal reading is strong as a function of the selective order, but immediate terror, labor control, and political intimidation remain possible co-purposes.
The tower and ع ن د activations are root-network resonances and should not be promoted into literal lexical claims.
The focus states that the women are kept alive; it does not itself specify their later status or use.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Selective survival is part of the coercive plan.** `ح ي ي/B006` gives sparing alive, positioned against `ق ت ل/B001`, putting to death. Gendered objects make the contrast programmatic. I infer that killing and sparing are coordinated instruments for restructuring a community; “let the women live” reads as controlled preservation, not mercy.
2. **The plan loses its own aim.** `ك ي د/B001` supplies forceful handling, while `ض ل ل/B001` supplies deviation from aim. The restrictive conclusion encloses the first inside the second. I infer that intense manipulation cannot secure direction; the ayah reads the scheme as effort whose mechanism generates its failure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The believer’s protection and Pharaoh’s surrounding punishment in 40:45 disclose the eventual reversal of this population-control scheme.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The selective plot attacks continuity yet misses its own aim.** Lexically, `ك ي د:B002` is "plotting and stratagem," `ض ل ل:B001` is going astray from guidance and aim, and `ب ن ي:B007` is filiation and derived belonging. Structurally, the command targets believers' sons while retaining their women; 40:26 narrows the violence to Musa, and 40:28 reveals belief surviving inside Pharaoh's own household. Filiation's role is the channel the plan tries to interrupt. The packet gives selective killing and a hidden household believer; I infer that the strategy aims to sever transmission and that its internal survivor demonstrates mis-aim. `في ضلال` thus describes a plan structurally lost from its objective, not only morally wrong.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:45 completes the plot's mis-aim: the concealed believer is protected and harm surrounds the very household from which the strategy issued.

baseline.text: Musa onlara katımızdan gerçeği getirince, Onunla birlikte inananların oğullarını öldürün, kadınlarını sağ bırakın, dediler. İnkâr edenlerin tuzağı yalnızca boşa gider.

findings.text: Oğulları öldürüp kadınları sağ bırakmak, merhamet değil, bir topluluğun devamını ve yapısını denetlemek için birlikte kullanılan seçici araçlardır.
Yoğun biçimde yön vermeye çalışan tuzak, hedeflediği soy aktarımını kesemediği için kendi amacından sapar ve işleyişi başarısızlığını üretir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 Coercive Force and Protective Holding
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Political force attempts to seize and destroy, while refuge works by holding the threatened subject out of that force's reach.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Refuge is rendered as a retaining rope, barrier, or protective binding that counters coercive control.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Violence as Sovereign Control
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A ruler deploys killing, compulsion, and domination as instruments for controlling belief and public order.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: killing `quranic:root_001200:B001/m01`; exposing a target to killing `quranic:root_001200:B005/m01`; coercion or compulsion `quranic:root_000216:B003/m01`; dominating force `quranic:root_000732:B001/m01`; sovereign authority `quranic:root_000732:B003/m01`; warlike plotting `quranic:root_001334:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The order to kill is one operation in a larger apparatus: sovereign force tries to compel a public settlement by eliminating the dissenter.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 Proof and Doubt as Competing Materials
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Evidence seeks stable, penetrative clarity while doubt encloses, interlocks, and disturbs reception.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Proof becomes a solid straight object or sharp edge, whereas doubt behaves like piercing threads and enclosing armor.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Clear Proof with a Hard Edge
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A disclosed sign arrives as stable truth backed by an overpowering and verbally sharp proof.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: clear disclosure or evidence `quranic:root_000170:B004/m01`; revealing meaning in a sign or speech `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`; truthful statement `quranic:root_000852:B001/m01`; solid straight object `quranic:root_000852:B002/m01`; complete stable rightness `quranic:root_000852:B003/m01`; overpowering proof `quranic:root_000732:B002/m01`; sharp tongue `quranic:root_000732:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Evidence is both disclosure and resistant material. Its straightness lets it bear weight; its edge lets it cut through the opposing account.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Guidance places a leader and direction at the head of a road; straying removes both route and recoverable position.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Error extends from wrong direction to disappearance, burial, and lost possession.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Straying until the Object Vanishes
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A traveler misses the goal, drops from view, and becomes like a possession whose location can no longer be recovered.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: straying from the goal `quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`; vanishing or burial `quranic:root_000913:B002/m01`; lost possession `quranic:root_000913:B003/m01`; stray animal `quranic:root_000913:B005/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Misguidance is intensified from a route error into loss of locatability. The subject is not simply on another road but progressively absent from a recoverable course.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bu dalı yanlışın karşıtı olan doğruluk, gerçekliğe uygunluk, kesin olarak bilme ve sözün gerçek anlamında kullanılması çevresinde kurar. Verilen dal kimliği bu ortak çekirdeği doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, bir şeyin gerçekliğe uygun ve doğru oluşunu anlatır; çekişme, yükümlülük ve kişiye ait pay bu dalın dışında kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın kullanımlar doğruluk ve gerçekliğe uygunluk çekirdeğini taşır; yemin bildiren kalıp yalnız kendi söz dizimi içinde değerlendirilir ve dalın genel anlamına katılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşüncenin, sözün ya da durumun gerçekten var olana uygun düşmesi ve bu nedenle yanlışın karşısında doğru, sağlam ve kesin sayılmasıdır. Söz bakımından ayrıca eğretilemenin karşısındaki gerçek anlamı kapsar.

facets.statement: Gerçekte var olana uygun düşen şey doğru ve sağlamdır.
Bir konuyu araştırıp doğruluğundan kesin biçimde emin olma bu çekirdeğin bilgi alanındaki uzantısıdır.
Bir sözün eğretileme olmadan ilk konulduğu anlamda kullanılması, dil alanındaki özel görünümüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, yanlışın karşısındaki doğruluğu gerçekliğe uygunlukla açıklar; kesin olarak öğrenmeyi ve sözün eğretilemesiz gerçek anlamını da aynı anlam alanına bağlar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir düşüncenin, sözün veya durumun gerçekten var olana uygun ve yanlışın karşıtı olduğunu bütün çekirdeğiyle anlatmak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gerçekliğe uygunluk, doğruluk ve kesinlik öğelerinin tümünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sözün ya da yargının yanlış olmadığını belirten günlük bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Yanlışın karşısında bulunma ve gerçekliğe uygunluk yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Kesin bilgi ile gerçek anlam kullanımını tek başına belirtmez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sözün eğretileme değil, ilk ve doğrudan anlamında kullanıldığını belirtirken uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dilsel kullanımın eğretilemesiz ve yerli yerinde oluşunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel doğruluk ve kesin bilgi yönlerini kapsamaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin gerekli ve bağlayıcı hale gelmesini, bir kişinin ona layık ya da onunla yükümlü olmasını, ayrıca gerekli kılma ve hak etme işlemlerini birlikte verir. Dal çerçevesi bu ilişkileri doğru toplar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek, bir işin bağlayıcı biçimde gerekli olması veya bir sonucun kişiye düşmesidir; yalnızca doğru olma ya da özel mülkiyet payı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ve türemiş biçimler gereklilik ile hak edişi taşır; belirli ilgeç ve söz öbeklerine bağlı yönler kendi kalıplarında tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir işin yapılması zorunlu olacak biçimde bağlayıcı hale gelmesi veya bir kişinin bir yükümlülüğe, sonuca ya da karşılığa layık duruma gelmesidir. Buna gerekli kılma ve sonucu kendi davranışıyla üzerine çekme de dahildir.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin gerekli hale gelmesi, artık kaçınılamayan bir bağlayıcılık doğurur.
Bir kişinin bir işi yapmaya layık veya onunla yükümlü olması aynı ilişkinin kişi yönüdür.
Bir şeyi gerekli kılmak ya da bir sonucu davranışla hak etmek, durumun ettirgen ve dönüşlü uzantılarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, gereklilik ve bağlayıcılığı kişi açısından layık olma, yükümlü tutulma, gerekli kılma ve bir sonucu hak etme yönleriyle bir araya getirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin zorunlu hale gelmesini ve buna bağlı yükümlülük ya da hak ediş ilişkisini birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Gerekli olma, bağlayıcılık, yükümlülük ve hak ediş yönlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir iş veya hüküm artık yapılması gereken bağlayıcı bir duruma geldiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Kişinin bir karşılığa layık olması ve gerekli kılma yönlerini kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin davranışı nedeniyle bir sonuç veya karşılığa layık hale gelmesini anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Sonucun kişiye bağlanması ve layık hale gelme yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel gereklilik ve başkasını yükümlü kılma yönlerini kapsamaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişiye ait olan özel istemi veya payı, bunun başkasına karşı ileri sürülmesini ve kişiye öncelik vermesini açıkça anlatır. Dal kimliği bu sahiplik ilişkisini korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Burada genel zorunluluk değil, belirli bir sahibin isteyebileceği özel pay, yetki veya öncelik söz konusudur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçimler kişiye ait payı bildirir; bir malın başkasının elinden hükümle alınmasını anlatan kullanım kendi işlem bağlamında tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Belirli bir kişiye ait olan, sahibinin başkasından isteyebildiği veya başkasına karşı ileri sürebildiği özel pay, yetki ya da önceliktir. Bu bağın tanınıp malın sahibine geçirilmesi de aynı alanın işlem yönüdür.

facets.statement: Özel pay veya yetki belirli bir sahibine bağlıdır ve onun tarafından istenebilir.
Birden çok isteyen arasında bir kişinin daha öncelikli sayılması sahiplik ilişkisinin özel görünümüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, genel bir doğruluktan daha özel olarak kişiye ait payı, bu paydaki önceliği ve sahibinin başkasına karşı sahiplik bağını kurmasını anlatır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişinin kendisine ait sayılan şeyi isteme, elde tutma veya öncelikle geri alma bağını eksiksiz anlatmak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Belirli sahip, özel pay, isteme yetkisi ve öncelik öğelerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir mal, alacak veya yetkinin belirli bir kişiye ait olduğunu belirtirken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Belirli bir sahibine bağlı özel pay oluşunu korur.
error_profile.loses: İsteme işlemini ve yarışan kişiler arasındaki önceliği açıkça göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birden çok kişi arasından birinin geri alma veya isteme bakımından önde olduğunu açıklarken uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Sahibe bağlı isteme yetkisi ve öncelik yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Özel payın bütün sahiplik ve aktarım alanını kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: sahibine ait ve onun isteyebileceği özel pay
malı, elinde tutana karşı kendisinin saydırıp geri aldı

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal her tür özel pay, isteme yetkisi ve kişiler arasındaki önceliği kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yalnızca bir evde bulunan sabit pay veya paydaşlık bağını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: özel pay ile evdeki sabit pay
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da belirli bir kişiye bağlı, yerleşmiş bir payı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal ev bağlamına daralmış bir örnektir; odak dal ise mal, istem ve öncelik ilişkilerini genel olarak kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kişiye ait olan payın veya yetkinin kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal o payı karşı taraftan sürekli isteme ve tahsil etmeye çalışma eylemidir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: sahip olunan pay ile onu isteme
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir kişinin başkasından isteyebileceği bir şey bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal istemin dayanağı olan sahiplik bağını, komşu dal ise bu bağa dayanarak yapılan isteme ve alma sürecini anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Tüm komşular incelendi; evdeki sabit payla yakınlık ve payın kendisiyle onu isteme eylemi arasındaki ayrım en yararlı karşılaştırmalar olarak seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الحق والحقوق والحقة بمعنى الحق الخاص، والأحقية بين أصحاب المطالبة، والاستحقاق بمعنى ملك الحق على غيره.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مطلق الوجوب بلا صاحب حق، ولا الخصومة نفسها إلا من جهة محل الحق المتنازع عليه.
branches.source_phrase_ar: إنك لتعرف الحقة عليك (maqayis)؛ الحق واحد الحقوق والحقة أخص منه، هذه حقتي أي حقي (sihah;tahdhib)؛ استحقها على المشتري أي ملكها عليه (tahdhib)؛ وبعولتهن أحق بردهن (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinde tarafların çekişmesi, her birinin doğrunun veya payın kendisinde olduğunu ileri sürmesi ve kimi kullanımda bir tarafın üstün gelmesi açıkça yer alır. Dal kimliği bu karşılıklı yapıyı doğru verir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek, iki ya da daha çok tarafın aynı doğruluk veya pay iddiasıyla karşı karşıya gelmesidir; çekişmesiz doğruluk bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Karşılıklı çekişme türemiş biçimlerde görülür; küçük işler üzerinde çok çekişmeyi anlatan söz öbeği yalnız o özel kullanımda korunur.

concept_map.definition: İki ya da daha çok tarafın aynı konuda doğru tarafın veya istenen payın kendilerinde olduğunu ileri sürerek birbirleriyle çekişmesidir. Süreç, bir tarafın savını kabul ettirip üstün gelmesiyle sonuçlanabilir.

facets.statement: Taraflar karşılıklı olarak çekişir ve her biri kendi savının doğru olduğunu ileri sürer.
Çekişmenin sonunda bir tarafın savını kabul ettirerek ötekine üstün gelmesi olası sonuçtur.
Önemsiz ve küçük konularda durmadan çekişme, kalıba bağlı özel bir kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, karşılıklı çekişmeyi tarafların doğrunun kendilerinde olduğunu ileri sürmesiyle açıklar; üstün gelme ve küçük işler üzerinde aşırı çekişme bunun özel yönleridir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Tarafların aynı konuda kendi savlarını doğru sayarak karşılıklı biçimde çatışmasını bütün kurucu öğeleriyle anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılıklı tarafları, doğruluk savını, çekişmeyi ve olası üstün gelmeyi korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İki tarafın aynı payın kendilerine ait olduğunu ileri sürerek tartıştığı bağlamlarda doğaldır.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılıklı sav ileri sürme ve çekişme yapısını korur.
error_profile.loses: Doğruluk savının daha geniş alanını ve üstün gelme sonucunu kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir çekişmenin sonunda taraflardan birinin kendi savını geçerli kıldığı bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Çekişmede savı kabul ettirerek üstün gelme sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Karşılıklı çekişmenin bütün sürecini ve küçük işler kalıbını kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: doğrunun kendisinde olduğunu ileri sürerek onunla çekişti
karşılıklı çekişip her biri kendini doğru saydı
çekişmede savını kabul ettirip üstün geldi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda her taraf özellikle doğrunun veya istenen payın kendisinde olduğunu ileri sürer.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal her türlü karşılıklı anlaşmazlığı ve sözlü mücadeleyi daha genel biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: doğruluk savlı çekişme ile genel çekişme
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da karşı karşıya gelen tarafların birbirleriyle çekişmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın ayırıcı koşulu tarafların doğruluk veya pay savıdır; komşu dal bu koşul olmadan da her tür çekişmeye uygulanabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal tarafların karşılıklı çekişme ve sav ileri sürme eylemidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal çekişmeye konu olabilen kişisel payın veya isteme yetkisinin kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Kişiye ait bir pay, iki dalın da yer aldığı aynı anlaşmazlık ortamında bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Burada olayın kendisi, komşu dalda ise olayın konusu ve sahibine bağlı dayanak anlatılır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; genel çekişmeden ayıran doğruluk savı ile çekişme konusu olan özel pay arasındaki iki sınır yayımlandı.
branches.branch_image_ar: محاقة يدعي كل طرف فيها الحق
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه حاقه وحاققته وتحاق القوم واحتقوا، أي تخاصموا وادعى كل واحد أن الحق معه، ومنه نزق الحقاق.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الحق الثابت بلا نزاع، ولا إحقاق الحق بإظهاره.
branches.source_phrase_ar: حاق فلان فلانا إذا ادعى كل واحد منهما (maqayis)؛ حاقه أي خاصمه، والتحاق التخاصم والاحتقاق الاختصام (sihah)؛ تحاق القوم واحتقوا إذا تخاصموا (tahdhib)؛ حاققته فحققته أي خاصمته في الحق فغلبته (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnız başkasına kanıt göstermeyi değil, bir konudan kesin olarak emin olmayı, bir söz veya sanıyı doğrulamayı, doğru olduğunu bildirmeyi ve doğru diye belirlemeyi de içerir. Dal korunabilir, ancak gösterme işlemi bu daha geniş doğrulama alanının yalnız bir yönüdür.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, doğruluğu belirleme, onaylama veya gösterme işlemlerini kapsar; bir şeyin kendiliğinden doğru olma durumu ayrı tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Türemiş biçimlerin doğrulama ve kesinleştirme yönleri birlikte korunur; söz ve sanı nesneleriyle kurulan özel kalıp bütün dala genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir konunun doğru olduğunu araştırıp kesin olarak belirlemek, doğru diye onaylamak veya kanıtlarla görünür kılmaktır. İşlem kişinin kendi kesinliğe ulaşmasından bir savı başkasına kabul ettirmesine kadar uzanabilir.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin doğru olduğunu belirleyip onu doğru diye onaylama işlemi çekirdeği oluşturur.
Araştırma sonunda kişinin kendisinin kesinliğe ulaşması işlemin bilgi yönüdür.
Doğruluğu kanıtlarla açığa çıkarıp bir savı geçerli kılma işlemin gösterme yönüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık, kesin olarak öğrenme, bir söz veya sanıyı doğrulama, doğru olduğunu bildirme ve kanıtlayarak geçerli kılma işlemlerini ortak bir doğrulama alanında birleştirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir konunun doğru olduğundan emin olma, onu onaylama ve gerektiğinde kanıtla görünür kılma sürecini birlikte anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Belirleme, kesinleşme, onaylama ve kanıtla gösterme yönlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sözün, sanının veya bilginin doğru olduğunu inceleyip onaylama bağlamlarında en doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Doğruluğu belirleyip onaylama işleminin temel yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Kişisel kesinliğe ulaşma ile kanıtları görünür kılma yönlerini açıkça söylemez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir savın kanıtlarla ortaya konup geçerli kılındığı tartışma veya yargı bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Doğruluğu başkasına görünür kılma ve geçerli saydırma yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Yalnız kişinin kendi kesinliğe ulaşması yönünü kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: sözünün veya sanısının doğru çıktığını gösterdi
savını geçerli kılıp karşısındakine üstün geldi
doğruyu söyledi veya doğru istemi kabul edildi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kişinin kesinliğe ulaşmasını ve bir söz ya da sanıyı doğrulamasını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kanıtın kendisini, yargıyla sabitlemeyi ve görme ya da düşünmeyle yerleşen bilgiyi de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir savın doğru ve geçerli sayılmasını sağlayan işlemleri anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal doğruluğu belirleme ve onaylama sürecine, komşu dal ise kanıt veya yargı yoluyla sabitlemeye daha belirgin biçimde yönelir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal doğruluğu araştıran, onaylayan veya gösteren etkin bir işlemdir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal bir şeyin zaten gerçekliğe uygun ve doğru olma durumudur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da doğruluk ve gerçekliğe uygunluk çevresinde buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal doğruluğun belirlenmesi veya gösterilmesini, komşu dal ise işlemin sonucundan bağımsız olarak doğru olma niteliğini anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün komşu kartları değerlendirildi; kanıtla sabitleme ile yakınlık ve doğrulama işlemiyle doğru olma durumu arasındaki ayrım yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أحققت وحققت بمعنى أثبت الحق أو حكمت بكونه حقا أو صدقت القول، وإحقاق الحق بإظهار الأدلة أو إكمال الأمر.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مجرد كون الشيء حقا دون فعل إثبات، ولا المخاصمة إلا إذا غلب وأثبت الحق.
branches.source_phrase_ar: حققت الأمر وأحققته أي كنت على يقين منه (maqayis)؛ حققت قوله وظنه تحقيقا أي صدقت (sihah)؛ حقق الرجل إذا قال هذا الشيء هو الحق (tahdhib)؛ أحققت كذا أي أثبته حقا أو حكمت بكونه حقا، ليحق الحق (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu sözü Son Gün için özel bir ad olarak verir ve adlandırmayı bütün işlerin gerçekleşmesi, herkesin yaptığıyla yüzleşmesi ya da karşılığın kesinleşmesiyle açıklar. Dal çerçevesi bu özel göndermeyi doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal genel bitiş veya zorunluluk değil, yapılanların karşılığının kesinleştiği Son Gün için kullanılan özel bir addır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal tek başına kullanılan özel bir olay adını tanımlar; başka söz öbeklerindeki bitiş, doğruluk veya zorunluluk anlamları buraya taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bütün işlerin gerçek sonucuna ulaştığı, her insanın yaptıklarıyla yüzleştiği ve karşılığın kesinleştiği Son Gün için kullanılan addır.

facets.statement: Ad, insanların yaptıklarıyla yüzleştiği Son Gün olayını gösterir.
Adlandırma, o günde işlerin gerçek sonucuna ulaşması ve karşılığın kesinleşmesiyle açıklanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık adı Son Günle özdeşleştirir; gerekçe olarak işlerin gerçekleşmesi, kişinin yaptığıyla yüzleşmesi ve karşılığın kesinleşmesi biçiminde birbirini tamamlayan açıklamalar sunar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bütün insanların yaptıklarıyla yüzleşeceği ve karşılıkların kesin biçimde verileceği son yargı gününü adlandırır.

error_profile.preserves: Özel gün göndergesini, yüzleşmeyi ve karşılığın kesinleşmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Dini veya öğretici bir metinde herkesin yaptıkları için yargılanacağı son günü belirtirken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Özel gün göndergesini ve insanların yaptıklarıyla yüzleşmesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Adın işlerin gerçekleşmesi ve karşılığın kesinleşmesi gerekçesini açıkça vermez.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bütün karşılıkların kesinleştiği Son Yargı Günü

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal genel olarak doğru, gerçek ve gerçekliğe uygun olma niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Adın açıklanmasında işlerin gerçek sonucuna ulaşması ve kesinleşmesi bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal tek bir gelecekteki olayı gösterir; komşu dal ise olay türünden bağımsız genel bir doğruluk ve gerçeklik niteliğidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal insanların yaptıklarıyla yüzleşeceği özel Son Günü gösterir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal herhangi bir işin tamamlanmasını, sona ermesini veya tükenmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: Son Gün ile genel sona erme
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de bir sürecin artık sonuçlandığı bir son aşama tasarımında buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal genel bir bitiş sürecidir; odak dal ise bitiş anlamından ibaret olmayan, yargı ve karşılık içeren özel bir gündür.
